structure: Part 7, Transporter, read at commit c2078fb in full: the four DR2.1 views transporter.html, transporter-add.html, transporter-add-private.html and transporter-add-commercial.html; the partials transporter-add-private-fields.html, transporter-add-commercial-fields.html and transporter-authorisation-banner.html; app/data/transporters.js (8 seeded transporters) and app/data/transporter-types.js (2 types); app/routes.js 3760-4367 (transporter search and results, render functions, template matching, type validation, private and commercial form parsing and validation, save to the session list and the address book, cancel redirect) and 14547-14880 (GET /transport-details, GET /transporter, GET and POST /transporter/add, /transporter/add/private, /transporter/add/commercial, POST /transporter). Read beside them for what these pages show: the shared postcode lookup handler (routes.js 4595-4699), hasJourneyUpdates (316-322), the address book country list (11955-11966) and the shared journey-form-actions partial. Pages covered: the Transporter details page (summary of the selected transporter with Change and Remove, or search and a radio table, live-animals-only authorisation guidance, success banner, journey actions); Choose a transporter type (2 options, 1 error); Add a private transporter as a 3-step UK postcode lookup (postcode, select an address, details); Add a commercial transporter as a 4-step flow (authorisation number, postcode, select an address, details) with the Northern Ireland-only country and the authorisation banner on its first step; every field label, hint, error message, cancel and how a new transporter reaches the transporter list or the address book. Changes since the earlier extract: the selected-transporter summary with Change and Remove, live-animals-only guidance, the postcode-lookup steps on both add pages (the commercial typeahead address search is gone), step-dependent commercial back links, and success messages now ending with a full stop. Earlier claims those changes made untrue were dropped and given new ids; every other earlier claim is kept with updated line references.

claims.statement: The select-an-address step has a 'Continue' button and an 'Enter address manually' link-style button.
On both add pages, choosing Continue on the select-an-address step without choosing an address shows the error 'Select an address', linked to the dropdown, and shows the list again.
On the private page, choosing an address fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, the formatted postcode and the country United Kingdom from it, and moves to the details step.
claims.quote:
addressLine1: chosenAddress.addressLine1 || '',
              addressLine2: chosenAddress.addressLine2 || '',
              townOrCity: chosenAddress.townOrCity || '',
              county: chosenAddress.county || '',
              postcode: postcodeLookupLocals.lookupPostcode,
              country: 'United Kingdom'
claims.note: The private name is not filled from the chosen address; the name the user typed is kept.

claims.statement: On the private page, 'Change postcode' goes back to the postcode step and 'Enter address manually' goes to the details step; both clear the address fields and any errors.
Both add pages show their primary 'Save and continue' button only on the details step; the cancel button shows on every step.
When the private form fails validation on save, the page is shown again at the details step with every error listed in field order in the summary and beside each field, and the entered values kept.
Under DR2.1 the add commercial transporter page has four steps: the transporter authorisation number, enter a postcode, select an address, then the name, address and contact details.
claims.quote:
With the address lookup (GOV.UK "Addresses" pattern) the page has four steps:
    transporter - authorisation number
    postcode - enter a postcode and select "Find address"
    results  - select an address from the dropdown list
    details  - name, address and contact details

claims.statement: The add commercial transporter page opens at the step named in the URL (?step=transporter or ?step=postcode), otherwise at the authorisation number step, and opening it by a link clears any errors.

The add commercial transporter page's back link depends on its step: from the authorisation number step it goes to the transporter type page, from the postcode step to the authorisation number step, and from the select-an-address and details steps to the postcode step.
The commercial authorisation number step shows only the 'Transporter authorisation number' field and a 'Continue' button (with the cancel button).
The add commercial transporter page shows the 'Important' transporter authorisation banner only on the authorisation number step, and not at all for a germinal products notification.
claims.quote:
{# The authorisation help sits with the authorisation number, on the first step #}

claims.note: The transporter page shows its guidance only for live-animals, while this banner shows for any type other than germinal-products: the two conditions differ.

claims.statement: The commercial authorisation banner is headed 'Help with transporter authorisation' and repeats the DAERA or APHA authorisation guidance, the economic-activity guidance link (opens in a new tab) and the DAERA and EU document validity statements.

claims.statement: Continue on the commercial authorisation number step checks only the authorisation number: if it is blank the step shows 'Enter a transporter authorisation number' again, otherwise it moves to the postcode step.
The commercial postcode step's 'Enter a UK postcode' field has the hint 'For example, BT1 5GS'.

The commercial page passes the Northern Ireland lookup addresses to the postcode lookup, but the lookup ignores that list and searches the same postcode lookup addresses as other pages, so a looked-up address need not be in Northern Ireland.
claims.note: mechanism: findPostcodeLookupAddresses takes one argument, so the sourceAddresses passed by buildPostcodeLookupResultItems are dropped. The country is still always saved as Northern Ireland.

claims.statement: On the commercial page, choosing an address fills the name (when the user left it blank) from the address's name or organisation, and fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and the formatted postcode, then moves to the details step.

On the commercial page, 'Change postcode' goes back to the postcode step with the values kept, and 'Enter address manually' goes to the details step with the address fields cleared; both clear any errors.
claims.quote:

claims.statement: The commercial details step shows 'Name or organisation name', the address fields, the disabled Northern Ireland country and the 'Enter contact details' section; on earlier steps the name and authorisation number are carried in hidden fields.
Each step of the commercial page keeps what has been entered so far in the session, so the back links and later steps show it.

claims.statement: When the commercial form fails validation on save, every error is listed in field order in the summary; the page returns to the authorisation number step if the authorisation number is missing, otherwise it stays on the details step with the errors beside each field and the entered values kept.

The prototype has no format validation for the transporter email address, phone number, the postcode typed in the address fields, or the commercial authorisation number: only the lookup postcode is checked as a UK postcode.
claims.note: Looked in validateTransporterPrivateForm, validateTransporterCommercialForm and getAddAddressPostcodeLookupLocals. Both form validators check only that each required field is present.
